pages.description: The Maintenance Order page lets you create and manage vehicle maintenance records in the U-Go garage system. Operations staff use this page to log maintenance work, assign it to specific vehicles and drivers, and request spare parts needed for the job. You'll use this whenever a vehicle comes in for routine service or repairs.
how_to_use: Select your preferred language using the dropdown at the top if needed.
Choose the vehicle that needs maintenance from the Vehicles dropdown.
Enter or select the driver's name associated with the vehicle.
Select the type of maintenance being performed (for example: oil change, tire rotation, inspection).
Enter today's date in the Maintenance Date field and record the current odometer reading in kilometers.
If spare parts are needed, click 'Add New' in the spare parts section and enter each part's details (model, part name, and quantity needed).
Click 'Submit' to save the maintenance order, or 'Submit Request' if you need manager approval for spare parts.

field_descriptions.Vehicles: Select the specific vehicle ID or plate number that requires maintenance. Use the dropdown to search if you have many vehicles.
field_descriptions.Driver_Name: Enter or select the driver currently assigned to this vehicle.
field_descriptions.Type_of_Maintenance: Choose from preset options like preventive maintenance, repairs, inspections, or emergency service.
field_descriptions.Type_of_Vehicle: Select the vehicle category (truck, van, car, etc.) — this may auto-fill based on your vehicle selection.
field_descriptions.Current Odometer ( Km ): Record the odometer reading in kilometers at the time of maintenance. This helps track service intervals.

tips: Always record the odometer reading before submitting — this is critical for maintenance scheduling and warranty tracking.
If you need spare parts that aren't in stock, use 'Submit Request' instead of 'Submit' so the approval workflow can process the order before work begins.

pages.description: The Purchase Orders page allows you to create and manage purchase orders for vehicle maintenance parts and services. Procurement staff use this form to request spare parts from suppliers, either by linking to existing maintenance orders or by manually entering items. This is where you initiate all purchasing activities in the garage maintenance system.
how_to_use: Enter or locate the Purchase Order ID if one already exists, or leave blank to generate a new one
Set the Purchase Order Type using the radio buttons to specify if this is a standard order or a special request
Add purchase items by clicking Add New in either the automatic items section (linked to maintenance orders) or the manual items section (for direct purchases)
For each item, enter the spare part name, supplier name, and brand name
Review the Total PO Cost to confirm all items and quantities are correct
Select an Approved_By person from the dropdown to assign approval responsibility
Click Submit to send the purchase order for processing

field_descriptions.Notes: Add any special instructions, delivery requirements, or details about this order that the supplier should know
field_descriptions.PO_Date: The date this purchase order is created; this date is used for record-keeping and supplier communication
field_descriptions.Status: Displays the current stage of the purchase order (Draft, Submitted, Approved, Ordered, Received, etc.)
field_descriptions.Total PO Cost: The combined cost of all items in this purchase order; system calculates this automatically
field_descriptions.Approved_By: Select the person responsible for approving this purchase order before it goes to the supplier

tips: Always verify supplier and brand names match your approved vendor list to avoid delivery delays and cost overruns
Use the automatic items section when possible to link purchases to specific maintenance jobs; this keeps your records organized and trackable
Check the Total PO Cost before submitting—if it exceeds your authorization limit, assign it to the appropriate approval person or manager

pages.description: The Auto PO Items page allows you to create and manage automatic purchase orders for spare parts needed in garage maintenance. Maintenance planners and procurement staff use this page to link spare parts to maintenance orders, set quantities and pricing, and track the procurement status. This is typically used when setting up reusable maintenance templates or processing bulk spare part requests.
how_to_use: Select the Maintenance Order Source from the dropdown to link this spare part to a specific maintenance job or template.
Choose the Spare Part you need to order using the search dropdown—the system will show all available parts in your inventory.
Enter the Required Quantity for this spare part.
Fill in Supplier Name and Brand Name to specify where and what brand you want to order.
Enter the Estimated Unit Price so the system can calculate the Total cost automatically.
Set the Status to 'Pending' or 'Approved' depending on whether this order is ready to process.
Click Submit to save the auto PO item and add it to your procurement queue.

field_descriptions.Maintenance_Order_Source: Select the maintenance order or job template that requires this spare part. This links the purchase order to a specific maintenance task.
field_descriptions.Spare_Part: Search for and select the spare part you need to order. Use the search box to find parts by name or code.
field_descriptions.Required Quantity: Enter the number of units needed for this maintenance order.
field_descriptions.Supplier Name: Enter the name of the supplier or vendor you want to order from.
field_descriptions.Brand Name: Enter the brand or manufacturer name of the spare part to ensure correct ordering.
field_descriptions.Estimated Unit Price: Enter the cost per unit. The Total will calculate automatically by multiplying this by the Required Quantity.
field_descriptions.Status: Set to 'Pending' if the order is still being prepared, or 'Approved' if it is ready for procurement to process.

tips: The Total field auto-calculates—do not manually edit it. If the total looks wrong, check your Estimated Unit Price and Required Quantity.
Always link an Auto PO Item to a Maintenance Order Source before submitting. Orders without a source will be rejected during approval.

pages.description: The Fuel Control page lets you track and manage fuel consumption for your vehicles. Operations staff use this form to record fuel entries, monitor fuel efficiency, and calculate operating costs. Use this page regularly to maintain accurate fuel records and identify consumption patterns or anomalies.
how_to_use: Select your vehicle from the Vehicle dropdown at the top of the form.
Enter the Normal Consumption Rate for that vehicle (in liters per kilometer or your standard unit).
Click 'Add New' to create a new fuel entry record.
Fill in the fuel entry details: date, driver name, and fuel amounts in the provided fields.
The system automatically calculates Total Liters, Average Consumption, and Cost Per KM based on your entries.
Review the calculated values to verify they match your actual fuel usage.
Click 'Submit' to save the fuel entry.

field_descriptions.Vehicle: Select the vehicle you are recording fuel for. Choose from your registered fleet.
field_descriptions.Normal Consumption Rate: Enter the expected fuel consumption rate for this vehicle under normal operating conditions. This is used to identify unusual fuel usage patterns.
field_descriptions.Total Liters: Automatically calculated total fuel amount for this entry. This field is read-only.
field_descriptions.Last Odometer: Enter the vehicle's odometer reading at the time of refueling.
field_descriptions.Average Consumption: Automatically calculated average fuel consumption rate based on distance traveled and fuel used. This field is read-only.
field_descriptions.Cost Per KM: Automatically calculated fuel cost per kilometer. Use this to monitor fuel expense efficiency. This field is read-only.

tips: Always record fuel entries immediately after refueling to ensure accurate odometer readings and prevent data entry errors.
If your Average Consumption is significantly higher than the Normal Consumption Rate, the vehicle may need maintenance—check tire pressure, engine condition, and fuel filter.

tips: If Average Consumption is significantly higher than Normal Consumption Rate, the vehicle may need maintenance—check the Maintenance Sub Forms to schedule a service.

Click Done when finished reviewing the summary.

field_descriptions.lang-select-dropdown: Choose the language for the page display. This is optional and defaults to your system language.

pages.description: The Worst Vehicles Report shows which vehicles in your fleet consume the most fuel and have the highest fuel costs. Operations managers use this page to identify problem vehicles that may need maintenance, driver retraining, or replacement. Check this report regularly to control fuel expenses and improve fleet efficiency.
how_to_use: Open the Worst Vehicles Report from the Fuel Management section.
Select a date range using the 'From' and 'To' fields to analyze fuel consumption over a specific period.
Use the Vehicle dropdown to filter results for specific vehicles, or leave it empty to see all vehicles.
Review the table to see which vehicles have the highest Total Fuel Cost and Actual Consumption rates.
Click the checkbox next to any vehicle row to select it for further action.
Export the report using the Export button to share with your maintenance or driver management team.
Use the Print button to create a hard copy for your records or team meetings.
tips: High Actual Consumption values often signal maintenance issues like poor tire pressure, engine problems, or transmission wear. Flag these vehicles for immediate maintenance inspection.
Always compare fuel costs alongside consumption rates—a vehicle may use more fuel simply because it travels more miles. Focus on vehicles with high consumption per mile.

pages.description: This page allows supervisors and managers to evaluate driver performance across four key areas: fuel efficiency, on-time delivery, safety incidents, and documentation compliance. Use this form monthly to record each driver's performance ratings and provide feedback. Completed evaluations help identify training needs and recognize top performers.
how_to_use: Select your preferred language from the dropdown at the top if needed.
Enter or select the driver name you are evaluating.
Enter or select the month and year being evaluated.
Enter or select your own name (the person conducting the evaluation).
For each performance category (Fuel Efficiency, On-Time Performance, Incidents, and Documentation), select the appropriate rating option that best matches the driver's performance.
In the comments field below each category, briefly explain the rating or note any specific examples.
Click Submit to save and send the evaluation.

field_descriptions.Driver: The name of the driver being evaluated. Click or type to search and select from your fleet roster.
field_descriptions.Evaluation_Month: The month and year for which you are submitting this performance review. Select from the calendar dropdown.
field_descriptions.Evaluated_by: Your name or the name of the supervisor conducting this evaluation. This identifies who is responsible for the assessment.
field_descriptions.Fuel_Efficiency: Rate the driver's fuel consumption against company benchmarks. Select from the available rating options (typically ranging from poor to excellent).
field_descriptions.On_Time_Performance: Rate how consistently the driver met delivery and appointment schedules during the evaluation period.
field_descriptions.Incidents: Rate the driver's safety and conduct record, including any accidents, violations, or customer complaints.
field_descriptions.Documentation: Rate the driver's compliance with required paperwork, logbooks, vehicle inspections, and administrative procedures.
field_descriptions.\u062a\u0639\u0644\u064a\u0642\u0627\u06: Arabic comment field. Provide specific examples, observations, or notes supporting the rating you selected for each category.

tips: Complete evaluations consistently each month on the same schedule so you don't miss any drivers or duplicate reviews.
Use the comment fields to document specific incidents or examples—this helps drivers understand feedback and protects your company if performance issues need to be addressed later.

pages.description: This page lets you register and manage individual vehicles in your fleet. You enter vehicle details like license plate, make, model, fuel type, and GPS tracking status. Operations staff use this when adding new vehicles to the system or updating existing vehicle information.
how_to_use: Enter the vehicle's license plate in both the Letters and Digits fields to match your actual plate format.
Select the vehicle type using the radio buttons (for example, van, truck, or car).
Enter the vehicle's make, model, and year of manufacture.
Provide the chassis number, engine number, and date of purchase for record-keeping.
Select your fuel type and enter the normal fuel consumption rate in km/L so the system can track fuel efficiency.
Indicate whether the vehicle has a GPS tracker installed.
Upload a photo of the vehicle, then click Submit to save the vehicle record.

field_descriptions.Vehicles_Type: Choose the category of this vehicle: van, truck, car, or other.
field_descriptions.Normal Fuel Consumption (Km/L): Enter the typical fuel efficiency for this vehicle model (kilometers per liter). This helps monitor fuel costs and performance.
field_descriptions.Fuel_Type: Select the fuel this vehicle uses: petrol, diesel, or alternative fuel.
field_descriptions.Latest Fuel Price: Enter the current price per liter for this vehicle's fuel type.
field_descriptions.Fuel_Vehicle: Confirm whether this vehicle uses fuel-based propulsion.
field_descriptions.UGO ID: Your company's internal identifier for this vehicle (if assigned).
field_descriptions.Octain ID: The octane rating or fuel specification identifier for this vehicle.
field_descriptions.Make: The manufacturer of the vehicle (for example, Ford, Mercedes, Volvo).
field_descriptions.Chassis Number: The unique chassis or VIN number of the vehicle.
field_descriptions.GPS_Tracker: Indicate whether this vehicle has an active GPS tracking device installed.
field_descriptions.Year of Manufacture: The year the vehicle was built.
field_descriptions.Model: The specific model name or number from the manufacturer.
field_descriptions.Engine Number: The serial number of the engine.
field_descriptions.License_Expiry_Date: The date when the vehicle's license or registration expires.

tips: Always separate your license plate into letters and digits exactly as shown on your vehicle registration—do not mix them in one field.
Keep fuel consumption records accurate; incorrect data will give misleading cost reports and maintenance alerts. Update the fuel price field when your supplier's rates change.

field_descriptions.Quantity In: The number of units received in this stock delivery or purchase.
field_descriptions.Quantity Remaining: How many units of this part are currently available for use.

field_descriptions.Batch_Date: The date this batch of parts was received or purchased.
field_descriptions.Source: The supplier or vendor who provided these parts (e.g., 'ABC Parts Ltd', 'Direct Manufacturer').
field_descriptions.Notes: Any additional information about the parts, such as condition, storage location, or special handling instructions.

pages.description: The Repair Details page is where you record information about vehicle repairs performed at your service centers. You'll use this form after a repair is completed to document what was fixed, who did the work, and how much it cost. This creates a maintenance record for your fleet management and invoicing.
how_to_use: Select the type of repair from the Repair_Type dropdown (for example: engine repair, brake service, or tire replacement).
Enter a clear description of the problem in the Problem Description field so future technicians understand what was wrong.
Choose the repair category that best matches the work performed using the Repair_Category dropdown.
Enter the mechanic's name and the service center name where the repair was completed.
Record the invoice amount from your service center bill or receipt.
Upload any supporting documents such as invoices or work orders using the file upload field.
Check the acknowledgment checkbox at the bottom and click Submit to save the repair record.

field_descriptions.Repair_Type: Select the main type of repair performed (examples: engine, transmission, suspension, electrical, brakes). This helps you track which systems need the most maintenance.
field_descriptions.Problem Description: Write a brief explanation of what was wrong with the vehicle and what symptoms it showed. Be specific so mechanics can reference this in the future.
field_descriptions.Repair_Category: Choose a category that groups similar repairs together (examples: preventive maintenance, emergency repair, routine service). This helps you analyze maintenance patterns.
field_descriptions.Repair_Done_By: Specify whether the work was completed by your in-house mechanic or an external service center.
field_descriptions.Mechanic Name: Enter the full name of the person who performed the repair.
field_descriptions.Service Center Name: Enter the name of the garage or service facility where the work was done.
field_descriptions.Invoice Amount: Enter the total cost of the repair including labor and parts, as shown on the invoice.

tips: Always keep your invoice or receipt handy when filling out this form so you enter the correct amount and can upload the document immediately.
Be detailed in the Problem Description field—vague descriptions like 'car broken' make it hard for future reference and can cause confusion about warranty claims or repeat issues.

To add a new spare parts transaction, click Add (or press Option + Shift + N) and enter Supplier Name, Contact Person, Phone, Unit Price, and Quantity
Attach any supporting documents like invoices or delivery notes using the File upload column, then click Done
tips: The numbered checkboxes represent individual spare part items in your system. Check only the items you want to modify to avoid accidental bulk changes to unrelated parts.
Always attach file documentation (invoices, receipts) when recording transactions—this protects your records during audits and helps resolve supplier disputes quickly.

pages.description: The All Fuel Entries page displays a complete record of every fuel purchase across your vehicle fleet. Operations staff use this page to track fuel expenses, monitor fuel efficiency trends, and verify that fuel costs match your budget. Access this page regularly to review spending patterns and identify vehicles with unusual consumption.
how_to_use: Open the Fuel Management section and select 'All Fuel Entries' to view the complete fuel log
Use the table to review fuel records by Date, Driver, Odometer Reading, Fuel Quantity, and Total Fuel Cost
To filter or select specific entries, check the checkboxes next to the fuel records you want to work with
Use 'Bulk Edit' to update multiple fuel entries at once, or 'Export' to download fuel data for accounting or analysis
Click 'Print' to generate a fuel report for your records or to share with management
Use 'Delete' to remove incorrect fuel entries (do this only if the entry was entered in error, not to adjust historical data)
Click 'Done' when finished reviewing or making changes to return to the main menu
tips: Always record the odometer reading at the exact moment of fueling—delays in recording can create gaps in your distance calculations and make fuel efficiency reports inaccurate.
Use 'Export' at the end of each month to create a backup of all fuel entries and share detailed cost reports with accounting or fleet management.

pages.description: The Request Spare Parts Report page lets you view, manage, and request spare parts needed for vehicle maintenance. Garage operations staff use this page to track which parts are required, update quantities, and generate reports for ordering or inventory purposes.
how_to_use: Select your preferred language from the lang-select-dropdown at the top if needed.
Review the table to see all spare parts currently listed with their quantities and prices.
Check the checkboxes next to the spare parts you want to include in your report or request.
Update the Quantity Needed field for any parts where the amount has changed since the last entry.
Click the Print button to generate a printable report, or Export to save the data to a file.
Click Done when you have finished making changes and are ready to submit your request.
tips: Always verify quantities are correct before printing or exporting the report—incorrect amounts can delay maintenance schedules and affect inventory planning.
Use the Bulk Edit button if you need to update multiple spare parts at once, or the Duplicate button to copy a request for similar maintenance jobs.

pages.description: The Automation Control page lets garage maintenance staff set up and manage automated maintenance schedules and support requests. Use this page to configure when maintenance tasks run automatically and to connect with support staff when you need help troubleshooting issues.
how_to_use: Select your preferred language from the lang-select-dropdown if you need to change the interface language.
Enter the time you want automated maintenance to run in the Next_Run_Time field (for example, 02:00 for 2 AM).
Check the 'useIconSwitch' checkbox if you want to use custom icons for your automation displays.
Click 'saveIcons' to save your icon settings, or 'resetIcons' if you need to restore the default icons.
If you need support, enter your email address in the reqEmailId field and select a support type from the supportType dropdown.
Check the box 'I have read the above conditions' to confirm you understand the support terms.
Click 'Submit Request' or 'reachUsStartChat' to send your support request or open a chat with the support team.

field_descriptions.Next_Run_Time: Enter the specific time (in 24-hour format, like 14:30) when you want the automated maintenance tasks to start running.

tips: Always check the 'I have read the above conditions' box before submitting a support request — the system will not process your request without this confirmation.
When describing your support issue, include the exact time the problem happened and what maintenance task was running — this helps support staff respond faster and more accurately.

pages.description: The All Automation Controls page lets you manage scheduled maintenance tasks and automation rules for your garage operations. Use this page to set up, modify, and monitor automated maintenance reminders, notification schedules, and system preferences. Operations staff access this when configuring how and when the system alerts them about upcoming vehicle maintenance.
how_to_use: Select your preferred language from the lang-select-dropdown if needed for the interface
Use the search field to find a specific automation rule or maintenance schedule by name or ID
Check the checkbox next to 'Next Run Time' if you want to filter or sort automation tasks by their scheduled dates
Set your desired date range using the 'From' and 'To' fields to view automations scheduled within that period
Adjust the volume slider to control notification intensity or alert frequency for the selected automation
Click Done to save your settings, or use Remove Changes to discard unsaved edits
Click Export or Import to back up your automation rules or apply configurations from another system

field_descriptions.From: Enter or select the start date to filter automations scheduled on or after this date
field_descriptions.To: Enter or select the end date to filter automations scheduled on or before this date

tips: Always set a clear date range before running bulk operations like Export or Duplicate—this prevents accidentally copying automations you don't need
If you enable edit permission for support staff, remember to disable it again once troubleshooting is complete for security reasons
